2. [LDET.5.3] **Refraction is suppression, not an ordering key.** An
   activation whose (rule, token) identity has already fired in this
   cycle is **not eligible to fire again** until its LHS changes. It is
   removed from consideration; it is not sorted later.

   In the CLIPS model, refraction is an axis in the conflict-resolution
   strategy. Here selection happens first and suppression is applied to
   the winner, so a refracted activation never competes at all.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__tick_keeps_activation_clocked
idris.note: An activation that fired and still matches after the tick is the same (rule, token) identity with its flag: it stays suppressed, as the clause requires until its LHS changes.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__window_2367_clocked
idris.note: Refraction across the window's two openings: one firing per opening and none while the activation persists, `[0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]`, computed.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_sorted
idris.note: Refraction is not an ordering key: setting `fired` moves no activation.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_chain_ordered
idris.note: Suppression by the flag leaves a rule's agenda order.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__mark_net_ordered
idris.note: Suppression by the flag leaves every rule's agenda order.

idris.name: Iret_11_3__sound
idris.note: The clause's rule as an invariant: an identity that fired and whose LHS has not changed is an activation carrying `fired`, and the set adds nothing to that.

idris.name: iret_11_3__refraction_after_history
idris.note: The clause's 'until its LHS changes' is the reading the theorem defends: an identity that fired is refused until its activation ends, and the set of [IRET.11.3.2], cleared more often, refuses nothing more. A set cleared only per pump ([LTIM.2.5.1] read strictly) would differ observably -- a match blocked by an RHS emit and released by a later RHS withdraw within one pump would be refused, against this clause.

idris.name: iret_11_3__select_spec_agrees
idris.note: Selection first, suppression on the winner: with the set subsumed by the flag, the suppression never changes the winner.

idris.name: ldet_5_8__tick_keeps_activation
idris.note: A TICK IS NOT A CHANGE TO THE LHS: an activation whose match the new test still admits is the same record after the tick, its `fired` flag included. A fired match stays refracted across every tick that leaves it matching -- Rete/NetworkRefraction.idr's theorem, restated under ticks.

tla.name: ldet_5_3__Readings
tla.note: Five readings of the suppression rule. `own` -- the flag, held until the activation is re-created -- is this clause; `runentry` is observably the same in the fragment. `pump` and `anywm` are readings the clause refuses, and `pump_oneshot` is libds, which agrees with `own` on every stream but one: the hash collision under the hash-alone key [IRET.11.3.3] refuses. On `tick_edge_twice`, where a gate that closes and reopens fires again (1@2 1@6, what [LTIM.2.5.1] requires of a reopening), libds's one-shot ends with the closing and it fires with `own`.

tla.name: ldet_5_3__libds_fires_each_opening
tla.note: LIBDS'S CELL ON THE REOPENING STREAM IS THE CLAUSE'S: the `pump_oneshot` reading fires 1@2 1@6 on `tick_edge_twice`, its one-shot ending with the closing as the flag does ([LTIM.2.5.1]), so the second opening fires. One cell of the table held on its own so that it carries its own verdict; the engine that keeps the one-shot past the closing breaks it (the `.teeth.oneshot_outlives.` config, held on every run of the lane).

tla.name: ldet_5_3__table_holds
tla.note: Within the model's streams (TLC, every reading x identity x stream). The `pump_oneshot` column is libds: its refraction table is keyed by a cycle generation that advances on every working-memory assert and retract and once per pump, so a match blocked and released within one pump fires again (stream `same_pump_rel`, 1@1 1@1), as this clause requires; and its one-shot for a time-dependent rule ends with the closing, so a reopened gate fires again (`tick_edge_twice`, 1@2 1@6, as [LTIM.2.5.1] requires; `ldet_5_3__libds_fires_each_opening`). libds differs from the clause's column in one place: under the hash-only identity it still uses in RT mode, which [IRET.11.3.3] forbids in every mode.
